Noah (Design): Quick design review: proposing a "stripline" component that sits between timepicker and heatmap — shows p50/p95 sparkline + throughput bars in one row. Focus: quick scan and lightweight actions (pin, inspect). Thoughts?
Ivy (Frontend): Looks promising. Concern: combining bars + sparklines may be cramped at narrow widths. Maybe allow collapse into a single compact mode.
Liam (Product): Main need: reduce time-to-signal when ops are triaging. If stripline lets them jump-to-range and toggle sampling, that's huge. Keep actions minimal.
Chloe (A11y): Accessibility note: action icons need accessible names and focus order. Also ensure color is not sole indicator for anomaly state. Use icons + patterns.
Ethan (Eng Runtime): Backend can emit 30s aggregates for stripline which balance fidelity and cost. We'll add a param ?resolution=30s.
Noah (Design): For compact mode proposal: collapse percentile lines into a single gradient band and show tooltip with exact percentiles on hover/focus.
Ivy (Frontend): Tooltip-on-focus is fine, but avoid heavy DOM for every tile — render tooltip content lazily. Canvas for sparklines + SVG overlays for interaction?
Chloe (A11y): Canvas needs an accessible fallback. Provide an offscreen live region that reads out summary when focused: "p50 120ms, p95 420ms, throughput 300r/s".
Liam (Product): Copy question: for the pin action label should it read "Pin range" or "Save comparison"? Which is clearer for users?
Noah (Design): "Pin range" is shorter and maps to the UI affordance. We can surface "Saved comparisons" in a side drawer.
Ethan (Eng Runtime): When pinned, we should persist in user prefs with a soft cap (default 4). Will emit pinned metadata with the interval response.
Ivy (Frontend): Interaction nit: keyboard users expect Enter/Space to activate pin. Also add an ARIA-pressed state on toggle buttons.
Chloe (A11y): Yes — use role="button" aria-pressed and include aria-describedby that references the live region for summary.
Noah (Design): Sampling control idea: micro-toggle on stripline to switch between "full" and "sampled" preview. Micro-toggle needs clear state color and text fallback.
Liam (Product): Make sampled default for large orgs to reduce API costs, but surface a one-click "refresh full" for deep dives.
Ethan (Eng Runtime): We'll support a query param sample=true/false. Default sampled when range > 1h. Also add sampling-ratio to response.
Ivy (Frontend): For small screens hide throughput bars, show only percentile band + condensed action menu. Use progressive disclosure.
Chloe (A11y): Menu must be reachable via keyboard and pointer; avoid hover-only triggers. Also reduce tooltip delay to 200ms for keyboard discoverability.
Noah (Design): Microcopy: replace "Anomaly" with "Spike" in stripline badges — "Spike detected" reads more action-oriented. Opinions?
Liam (Product): Spike is good. Also add severity levels: info/warning/critical with accessible text.
Ethan (Eng Runtime): Severity derived from baseline z-score; we'll include severity tag in interval payload.
Ivy (Frontend): Performance note: composite stripline into one canvas layer with hit-testing map to avoid many DOM nodes. We'll prototype perf metrics.
ci-bot: CI: design-proto/stripline v2 -> staging passed (unit + a11y smoke) at 2024-09-18T09:12Z :white_check_mark:
Noah (Design): Action items: I will update Figma with collapsed/expanded variants and microcopy. Ivy to spike canvas prototype. Chloe to draft A11y spec (live region + keyboard matrix). Ethan to add interval resolution param and severity field. Liam will update PRD with sampling defaults.
Ivy (Frontend): Will drop prototype link by EOD and include perf numbers for scrubbing.
Chloe (A11y): I'll include SR walkthrough and example NVDA narration.
Ethan (Eng Runtime): I'll return a JSON example for the new interval payload for frontend to integrate against.
Noah (Design): Thanks team — we'll reconvene after prototypes.
